title: Trastuzumab-resistant breast cancer cells-derived tumor xenograft models exhibit distinct sensitivity to lapatinib treatment
author: Liu, Ruan, et al.
materials: Human BC cell lines SKBR3 and BT474 were obtained from the American Type Culture Collection (Manassas, VA). The trastuzumab-resistant sublines SKBR3-pool2 and BT474-HR20, derived from SKBR3 and BT474, respectively, were described previously [26, 27]. They were routinely maintained in the presence of 20μg/ml of trastuzumab. Cell line authentication was confirmed by Short Tandem Repeat (STR) analysis with PowerPlex® 18D System from Promega (Madison, WI, USA). All cell lines were free of mycoplasma contamination, determined by the MycoAlert™ Mycoplasma Detection Kit (Lonza Group Ltd. Basel, Switzerland) every six months. Cells were cultured with DMEM/F-12 (1:1) medium (Thermo Fisher Scientific) containing 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) (Thermo Fisher Scientific) in a 37°C humidified atmosphere containing 95% air and 5% CO2 and split twice a week.

steps.title: Obtain breast cancer cell lines
steps.instruction: Acquire human breast cancer cell lines SKBR3 and BT474 from ATCC, and the trastuzumab‑resistant sublines SKBR3‑pool2 and BT474‑HR20 as previously described.

steps.title: Maintain cells with trastuzumab
steps.instruction: Keep all cell lines continuously in culture medium supplemented with 20 µg ml⁻¹ trastuzumab.

steps.title: Authenticate cell lines by STR
steps.instruction: Confirm cell line identity using Short Tandem Repeat analysis with the PowerPlex® 18D System (Promega).

steps.title: Check mycoplasma contamination
steps.instruction: Test each cell line for mycoplasma every six months using the MycoAlert™ Mycoplasma Detection Kit (Lonza).

steps.title: Culture cells in defined medium
steps.instruction: Grow cells in a 1:1 mixture of DMEM/F‑12 medium (Thermo Fisher Scientific) containing 10 % fetal bovine serum (Thermo Fisher Scientific) at 37 °C in a humidified incubator with 95 % air and 5 % CO₂; split the cultures twice per week.
